# Under the hood

The agent protocol, breakpoint parking, the RegisterNatives hook, caches,
and the plugin test suite.

## The request protocol

The host posts requests as JSON. The agent replies with the same id:

```json
{"id": 7, "type": "eval", "params": {"source": "Process.arch"}}
```

```json
{"id": 7, "ok": true, "result": {"value": "x64", "type": "string"}}
```

```json
{"id": 7, "ok": false, "error": "some failure"}
```

Request types:

`ping`, `eval`, `memRead`, `memWrite`, `ranges`, `threads`, `modules`,
`exports`, `imports`, `symbols`, `bpSet`, `bpList`, `bpRemove`, `bpParked`,
`Fr.cont.<tid>`, `regRead`, `regWrite`, `wpSet`, `wpList`, `wpRemove`,
`isJavaAvailable`, `loaderList`, `classList`, `classLoadMonitor`,
`newlyLoadedClasses`, `rnSet`, `rnList`, `flagModules`, `classDescribe`.

The `Fr.cont.<tid>` type is how continuing works: a request whose type is
the parked thread's channel name.

## Asynchronous events

| Event | Payload |
|---|---|
| `agent.ready` | the agent booted (`version: 1`) |
| `Fr.bp` | `bp`, `address`, `threadId`, `context: {}` (intentionally empty) |
| `Fr.bp.err` | a breakpoint callback failed |
| `Fr.wp` | `threadId`, `pc`, `operation`, `address`, `watched`, full `context` |
| `Fr.rn` | `className`, `methods` (name, signature, address) |
| `Fr.rn.warn` | buffer full, oversized batch, null methods pointer |

Events queue in the host buffer. `Frmj` drains them.

## Breakpoint parking

`bpSet` attaches an `Interceptor.attach` whose `onEnter` sends the
`Fr.bp` event, saves `this.context` into a `stopped` map keyed by
thread id, and then blocks in `recv('Fr.cont.<tid>').wait()` until the
host posts that request. This makes per-thread continue deterministic and
keeps register writes targeting the right context.

```{mermaid}
sequenceDiagram
    participant H as host
    participant A as agent
    participant T as target thread
    T->>A: onEnter at breakpoint
    A->>H: Fr.bp {bp, address, threadId}
    A->>A: stopped[tid] = this.context
    A->>A: recv('Fr.cont.<tid>').wait()
    H->>A: Fr.cont.<tid> (or bpParked for the most recent)
    A->>T: continue
```

`Frgj` with no thread first asks the agent which thread parked most
recently (`bpParked`).

## The RegisterNatives hook

`rnSet` resolves ART's live `RegisterNatives` dispatch path:

1. read the `JNIEnv` function table from `JNI_GetCreatedJavaVMs` when
   possible, so spawn-time setup does not initialize `frida-java-bridge`
   while the process is still frozen
2. otherwise scan libart for a `RegisterNatives` symbol (skip `CheckJNI`
   wrappers)
3. otherwise read the table from `Java.vm.getEnv()`
4. only then report `javaUnavailable`

A per-thread depth guard records wrapper re-entry once. The interceptor
copies the native method table in `onEnter` and promotes the class
reference with the caller's `JNIEnv` in `onLeave`. It does not call Java,
look up class names, or `send()` while `RegisterNatives` is running.
`FrRNj` flushes pending entries, resolves class names and emits
`Fr.rn` events. `Froj` for a USB/remote spawn arms this hook and
resumes before returning (`rn` true if it armed). USB/remote still resume
if Java is unavailable (`rn` false). `FrRNj on` on a still-suspended
spawn also resumes.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[env table index 215] --> B[CheckJNI or JNI RegisterNatives]
    B -->|onEnter copies methods| C[rnPending]
    C -->|rnList flush| D[rnBuffer + Fr.rn event]
```

## Class monitor

`classLoadMonitor` is a polling diff: `start` snapshots
`Java.enumerateLoadedClassesSync()` into a "seen" set. If already
enabled, `start` does not re-snapshot. `newlyLoadedClasses` re-enumerates and reports
names not in the set, adding them. `stop` sets `loadClassMonitorEnabled`
false and does not clear the seen set. No classloader hooks are involved.

## Caches

The agent caches the module list and the memory range list. Requests for
either return `cached: true` from the cache. `eval` invalidates both, and a
`refresh` argument (or any argument) forces re-enumeration.

## Memory access

`memRead`/`memWrite` use `NativePointer.readByteArray`/`writeByteArray`
(after checking the address against the range cache). Hex encoding is
lowercase. `Frwj` wants an even-length hex string.

## The tests

The plugin's test suite runs without any device, from the plugin source
tree after a frida-enabled meson build:

```bash
$ meson test -C build-frida -j1 -t 6
```

![The test suite](img/under_the_hood/tests.png)

The seven tests cover: the URI parser, session lifecycle, protocol helpers,
the agent message protocol, the null backend's `frida_unavailable` replies,
command registration, and the agent script protocol (the agent JavaScript
run in a mocked frida environment with node).
